# CLI reference

Update GitHub/Gitea/Forgejo Actions, Go module, container image, npm and Cargo dependencies.

```
deps [command] [flags]
```

deps finds the dependencies of a repository (GitHub/Gitea/Forgejo Actions, Go modules, container images, npm packages, Rust crates, Python packages and custom-annotated versions), looks up newer versions, and either prints the changes as a diff (`plan`), writes them (`apply`), or pushes one branch and opens one pull request per dependency or group (`run`). Files are edited byte-exactly and never reformatted.

The configuration is read from `.deps.yaml` (or `.deps.yml`) in `--dir`; `deps schema` prints its JSON Schema. Results go to stderr, diffs and explanations to stdout. See `deps help output`, `deps help environment` and `deps help exit-codes`.

Hidden flags for profiling: `--cpuprofile <file>` writes a CPU profile, and `--memprofile <file>` writes an allocation profile on exit (pprof format).

## Global flags

Every command accepts these flags.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--concurrency` | int | `32` | maximum concurrent network requests and lookups per upstream; npm and OSV get twice as many, container registries half; at least 1 |
| `--config` | string | `""` | config file, which must exist (default: \<dir>/.deps.yaml, then .deps.yml, else built-in defaults) |
| `--dir` | string | `"."` | repository directory to scan |
| `--log-format` | string | `"text"` | log format: text, json; $DEPS_LOG_FORMAT replaces the default |
| `--log-level` | string | `"warn"` | log level: debug, info, warn, error; $DEPS_LOG_LEVEL replaces the default |
| `-v, --verbose` | bool | `false` | also print skipped dependencies (skip lines) |

## deps apply

Write the updates to the files, including go mod tidy, package-lock.json and Cargo.lock.

```
deps apply
```

Resolves every dependency, prints the same report as `deps plan` on stderr, and writes the changed files, including `go mod tidy` output (`go.mod`, `go.sum`), regenerated `package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `uv.lock`, `poetry.lock` or `Pipfile.lock`, `Cargo.lock` updated with `cargo update`, and the `--hash` lines of requirements files (pip-compile/`uv pip compile` output is regenerated from its header command, other files get the new release's hashes from the index). Post-processors run on temporary copies; a failed one drops that module's or lockfile root's changes and is reported as an error.

A dependency with updates in several PR buckets contributes one update to the files: the newest non-major one, else the lowest major. Its other updates are reported with `, separate PR`, as is the lock file maintenance update (`lockFileMaintenance`), which only `deps run` makes.

The platform is only detected from CI environment variables. Locally, lookups run without a platform token unless one of the token variables is set (see `deps help environment`).

### deps apply examples

```sh
deps apply && git diff --stat
```

## deps completion bash

Generate the autocompletion script for bash.

```
deps completion bash
```

Generate the autocompletion script for the bash shell.

This script depends on the 'bash-completion' package.
If it is not installed already, you can install it via your OS's package manager.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(deps completion bash)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	deps completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/deps

#### macOS:

	deps completion bash > $(brew --prefix)/etc/bash_completion.d/deps

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

### deps completion bash flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--no-descriptions` | bool | `false` | disable completion descriptions |

## deps explain

Explain the rules, candidates and decision for each matching dependency.

```
deps explain <name-glob>...
```

Resolves only the dependencies whose name matches any of the doublestar globs (the syntax of rule `names`, for example `'actions/*'` or `'k8s.io/*'`) and prints, per occurrence, the matching rules, the effective policy, the rejected candidates by reason and the resulting update. The report goes to stdout, one block per occurrence:

```
actions/checkout  .gitea/workflows/ci.yml:10  (github-actions, action, git-tags, tag)
  current   v7.0.1
  rules     none
  policy    pin=keep allow=- updates=major,minor,patch,digest,pin group=- schedule=always minAge=-
  candidates 68
  rejected  not newer: 58 (v7.0.1, v7.0.0, v6.1.0, ...)  precision: 7 (v7, v6, v5, ...)  invalid: 2 (v2-beta, v6-beta)  prefix: 1 (1.0.0)
  result    up to date

github.com/spf13/pflag  go.mod:28  (gomod, indirect, go, go)
  current   v1.0.10
  rules     none
  policy    pin=keep allow=- updates=major,minor,patch,digest,pin group=- schedule=always minAge=-
  result    skipped: ignored by default (indirect; enable with a rule setting ignore: false)
```

The header names the manager, dep type, datasource and versioning. The other lines in a block:

- `builtin   monorepo <name> -> group "<name> monorepo"` appears for monorepo members.
- `rules` lists the matching rules as `#<i> <fields>`, or `none` when no rule matched. Rules with `updateTypes` that applied to an update follow as `#<i> <fields> (applies to <type>)`.
- `policy` is followed by one `<type>: <policy>` line per such type. `versioning=` is appended when a rule set it.
- `rejected` groups versions by reason, most frequent first, with up to 3 newest examples each. Reasons include `ignored by rule #4 for major`, `outside allow /^\d+\.\d+$/`, `update type major not allowed`, `too new (released 2026-11-01, minimum 28 days)`, `older than current`, `prerelease`, `precision` and `not newer`.
- `result` reads `skipped: <reason>`, `error: <err>`, `up to date`, or one `update` line per PR bucket, for example `update v6.0.0 -> v7.0.1 (major, bucket major)`.
- Each advisory is printed as `security  <id>  <summary>  <url>`.

Errors go to stderr as `error   <msg>`. A glob that matches no dependency fails with `no dependency matches <globs>` (exit 1). No globs, or an invalid glob, exits 2.

### deps explain examples

```sh
deps explain 'actions/*'
deps explain 'k8s.io/**' github.com/spf13/cobra
```

## deps plan

Print the updates as a unified diff without writing files.

```
deps plan
```

Resolves every dependency and prints the report on stderr (see `deps help output`). Then writes a unified diff per changed file to stdout (`a/<path>` → `b/<path>`); `git apply` accepts it. Nothing is written to the repository.

Post-processors do not run, so `go.sum` and lockfile changes are missing from the diff; `plan` notes this with `note    go.sum changes are computed by apply/run`, `note    package-lock.json changes are computed by apply/run`, `note    Cargo.lock changes are computed by apply/run` and `note    .terraform.lock.hcl changes are computed by apply/run`. Use `deps apply` to get them.

A dependency with updates in several PR buckets contributes one update to the files: the newest non-major one, else the lowest major. Its other updates are reported with `, separate PR`, as is the lock file maintenance update (`lockFileMaintenance`), which only `deps run` makes.

The platform is only detected from CI environment variables. Locally, lookups run without a platform token unless one of the token variables is set (see `deps help environment`).

### deps plan examples

```sh
deps plan > deps.diff && git apply --check deps.diff
deps plan -v --dir ../other-repo
deps plan --config ci/deps.yaml --log-level info
```

## deps run

Push one branch and open or update one pull request per dependency or group.

```
deps run [flags]
```

Detects the platform (GitHub, Gitea or Forgejo, from the CI environment, else from the `origin` remote), resolves every dependency, builds one commit per group on a temporary index (no checkout; the working tree is never modified), pushes it with `--force-with-lease`, and creates or updates the PRs.

- PRs whose updates all automerge (config key `automerge`) get platform auto-merge requested.
- With `dependencyDashboard`, the dashboard issue is read first (its ticked checkboxes apply to this run) and written last.
- With `lockFileMaintenance`, one more PR on `<branchPrefix>lock-file-maintenance` refreshes every `Cargo.lock` (`cargo update`) and `.terraform.lock.hcl` (`terraform init -upgrade`); it is closed when the lockfiles are current.
- Obsolete PRs under `branchPrefix` are closed and their branches deleted, but only when the run had no errors.
- The local `HEAD` must be the tip of `origin/<base>`.

**Token:** `--token`, then `DEPS_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GITEA_TOKEN`, `FORGEJO_TOKEN`, then the password from `git credential fill` for the platform host. Without any token, `run` fails with `no token for <host>`, except with `--dry-run`, which uses the API anonymously. Git pushes use the checkout's credentials.

**Author precedence:** an explicitly set `--author-name`/`--author-email`, then `$DEPS_GIT_AUTHOR`, then the config key `gitAuthor`, then the defaults. Each field is resolved separately. An invalid `DEPS_GIT_AUTHOR` exits 2.

**Commit signing:** with `--signing-key` (or `$DEPS_SIGNING_KEY`), every commit deps creates is signed. The value is the private key itself, as a CI secret holds it, or the path of a file holding it; the format is detected from the armor header:

- `-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----`: SSH signature (`gpg.format=ssh`) with a `0600` temporary copy of the key; needs `ssh-keygen`.
- `-----BEGIN PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK-----`: OpenPGP signature; the key is imported once into a temporary `GNUPGHOME`; needs `gpg`.

Only keys without a passphrase are supported; a protected key fails before any work is done. The temporary key material is removed when `run` exits, also on errors and on SIGINT/SIGTERM. The key is logged at info by fingerprint only, as `commit signing format=ssh|openpgp key=<fingerprint>`. A value that is neither format nor a readable file exits 2; a missing `ssh-keygen`/`gpg` exits 1. The forge shows the signature as verified only when the committer (`gitAuthor`) is the key owner's verified email. Without a key, git's own configuration applies (`commit.gpgSign` and `user.signingKey` of the checkout).

**Trigger:** schedules (config key `schedule`) are matched against what started the run, not against the clock: `--trigger-schedule`, then `$DEPS_TRIGGER_SCHEDULE`, then `$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME` with the `schedule` field of the payload at `$GITHUB_EVENT_PATH`. `workflow_dispatch` and local runs without CI variables are in schedule for every group. `push` runs are outside every schedule: only groups without a schedule (and security updates) get new PRs; open PRs are refreshed per `updateNotScheduled`. Logged at info as `trigger event=<event> cron=<cron>`. The value of `--trigger-schedule` is validated as a 5-field cron; an invalid one exits 2.

**New-PR limit:** the minimum of `--max-new-prs` and the room left below `prConcurrentLimit`/`prHourlyLimit`, counting only the non-zero ones. Existing PRs are always updated.

**PR statuses** (the `pr` lines, see `deps help output`):

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `created` | new PR |
| `updated` | content changed or the PR was unmergeable; force-pushed and PR edited |
| `rebased` | unchanged content rebuilt on a moved base (`rebaseWhen: behind-base-branch`), or on request from the dashboard |
| `up-to-date` | nothing to do |
| `closed` | obsolete PR closed and branch deleted |
| `would-create`, `would-update`, `would-rebase` | `--dry-run` |
| `skipped: closed PR for this version` | an unmerged closed PR has the same branch and title (the dashboard's recreate checkbox overrides it) |
| `skipped: outside schedule` | the run was triggered by a cron that is not in the group's `schedule` (the dashboard's create checkbox overrides it) |
| `skipped: new PR limit reached` | a PR limit is exhausted (dashboard checkboxes override it) |
| `skipped: branch modified by someone else` | the branch tip's author is neither the bot nor in `gitIgnoredAuthors` (the dashboard's rebase checkbox discards those commits) |

**Automerge outcomes** (appended to the PR status, e.g. `created, automerge`):

| Outcome | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `automerge` | platform auto-merge requested (or already scheduled); the forge merges once required checks pass |
| `automerge enabled` | GitHub reports auto-merge enabled already; not requested again |
| `automerge pending` | Gitea/Forgejo cannot schedule it yet (mergeability check of a fresh push still running); the next run asks again |
| `automerge waiting for checks` | GitHub will not auto-merge (auto-merge disallowed, or nothing to wait for) and the PR is not mergeable yet or its statuses/check runs are not all green; the next run checks again |
| `merged` | GitHub fallback: merged directly, mergeable with all statuses and check runs green |
| `would-automerge` | `--dry-run` |

**Dashboard statuses** (the `dashboard` line): `created`, `updated`, `up-to-date` (body unchanged, not edited), `would-create`, `would-update` (`--dry-run`), and `skipped: issues disabled` (the repository has no issue tracker; not an error).

### deps run examples

```sh
# what would happen, without a token and without writes
deps run --dry-run -v
# what the run triggered by the Sunday cron would do
deps run --dry-run --trigger-schedule '0 0 * * 0'
# in CI (the action runs this with DEPS_TOKEN set)
DEPS_TOKEN=$TOKEN deps run -v --log-level info
```

### deps run flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--api-url` | string | `""` | API base URL (default: detected) |
| `--author-email` | string | `"deps-bot@noreply.invalid"` | commit author email (when not set: $DEPS_GIT_AUTHOR, then gitAuthor of the config, then the default) |
| `--author-name` | string | `"deps[bot]"` | commit author name (when not set: $DEPS_GIT_AUTHOR, then gitAuthor of the config, then the default) |
| `--base` | string | `""` | base branch (default: the repository's default branch) |
| `--dry-run` | bool | `false` | report what would change without pushing or calling write APIs (no PR, merge or issue writes); works without a token |
| `--max-new-prs` | int | `10` | maximum number of pull requests to create per run (0 = unlimited) |
| `--platform` | string | `"auto"` | forge type: auto\|github\|gitea\|forgejo (auto: from the CI environment, else the origin remote) |
| `--repo` | string | `""` | repository owner/name (default: detected) |
| `--signing-key` | string | `""` | sign deps' commits with this passphrase-less private key (OpenSSH or armored OpenPGP), given as the key itself or a file path (default: $DEPS_SIGNING_KEY) |
| `--token` | string | `""` | platform API token; git pushes use the checkout's credentials (default: $DEPS_TOKEN, $GITHUB_TOKEN, $GITEA_TOKEN, $FORGEJO_TOKEN, git credential helper) |
| `--trigger-schedule` | string | `""` | act as if the run was triggered by this workflow cron, overriding $GITHUB_EVENT_NAME/$GITHUB_EVENT_PATH (default: $DEPS_TRIGGER_SCHEDULE) |

## deps schema

Print the JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) of .deps.yaml.

```
deps schema
```

Prints the JSON Schema of `.deps.yaml`, reflected from the config types, with every key's description (`markdownDescription` holds the long form editors show on hover). Unknown keys are rejected (`additionalProperties: false`), as in the loader. The repository's `deps.schema.json` is this output.

### deps schema examples

```sh
deps schema > deps.schema.json
# then start .deps.yaml with:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=./deps.schema.json
```

## deps version

Print the deps version.

```
deps version
```

Prints the version set at build time with `-ldflags "-X main.version=<v>"` (`dev` otherwise). Release binaries print their tag, e.g. `v0.1.0`; the action prints it after download.

## Environment

Environment variables deps reads. Also shown by `deps help environment`.

| Variable | Used by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `DEPS_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GITEA_TOKEN`, `FORGEJO_TOKEN` | all | platform token, first non-empty wins; `run --token` takes precedence. `run` falls back to `git credential fill` for the platform host, and without any token fails with `no token for <host>` (except `--dry-run`). Sent to the platform host's lookups as Basic `x-access-token:<token>`. |
| `DEPS_GITHUB_COM_TOKEN` | all | token for github.com lookups when the platform is not github.com (avoids anonymous rate limits for actions and releases hosted on GitHub) |
| `DEPS_DEFAULT_ACTIONS_URL` | all | default host of `owner/repo@ref` actions (hostname, or a URL whose host is used); overridden by the config key `actions.defaultHost` |
| `DEPS_NODE_DIST_URL` | `node-version` datasource | base URL of a nodejs.org `dist` mirror (default `https://nodejs.org/dist`) |
| `TF_TOKEN_<host>` | `terraform-provider`, `terraform-module` datasources | registry token sent as `Authorization: Bearer` to `<host>` (dots as `_`, hyphens as `__`, e.g. `TF_TOKEN_app_terraform_io`), as the Terraform CLI reads it; takes precedence over the CLI config |
| `TF_CLI_CONFIG_FILE`, `TERRAFORM_CONFIG` | `terraform-provider`, `terraform-module` datasources | Terraform CLI config read for registry `credentials` blocks and the `credentials_helper`, replacing `~/.terraformrc` (`%APPDATA%/terraform.rc`); when set, the `*.tfrc`/`*.tfrc.json` files of `~/.terraform.d` (`credentials.tfrc.json`) are not read. `TERRAFORM_CONFIG` is the legacy name |
| `HOME`, `APPDATA` (Windows) | `terraform-provider`, `terraform-module` datasources | where the Terraform CLI config, `credentials.tfrc.json` and credentials helpers (`.terraform.d/plugins`) are found |
| `DEPS_GIT_AUTHOR` | `run` | commit author `Name <email>`; between the `--author-*` flags and the config key `gitAuthor` |
| `DEPS_SIGNING_KEY` | `run` | default of `--signing-key`: a passphrase-less OpenSSH or armored OpenPGP private key, or the path of a file holding one; deps signs its commits with it |
| `DEPS_TRIGGER_SCHEDULE` | `run` | default of `--trigger-schedule` |
| `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME`, `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` | `run` | run trigger and its payload (cron of `schedule` events); set by GitHub, Gitea and Forgejo runners |
| `DEPS_LOG_LEVEL`, `DEPS_LOG_FORMAT` | all | defaults of `--log-level`, `--log-format` |
| `NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY`, `npm_config_registry` | `npm` datasource | registry when no `.npmrc` sets one (default `https://registry.npmjs.org/`) |
| `DOCKER_CONFIG` | `docker` datasource | directory of the Docker `config.json` with registry credentials and credential helpers (default `~/.docker`) |
| `DEPS_CRATES_INDEX_URL`, `DEPS_CRATES_API_URL` | `crate` datasource | base URLs of a crates.io sparse index mirror (default `https://index.crates.io`) and of the crates.io API used for source repositories (default `https://crates.io`) |
| `CARGO_HOME`, `CARGO_REGISTRIES_<NAME>_INDEX`, `CARGO_REGISTRIES_<NAME>_TOKEN`, `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` | `crate` datasource | alternative registries: Cargo's config (`$CARGO_HOME/config.toml`, default `~/.cargo`, after the `.cargo/config.toml` files from the manifest up to `--dir`) and credentials (`$CARGO_HOME/credentials.toml`); the variables override them as in Cargo. A registry token is sent as `Authorization` only to its index host; without one, the platform token (for its host) and, after a 401, `git credential fill` are used |
| `PIP_INDEX_URL` | `pypi` datasource | index when the manifest names none (simple API, JSON or HTML) |
| `PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL` | `pypi` datasource | space-separated extra indexes searched for every Python dep after the manifest's own; their releases are merged in |
| `DEPS_PYPI_URL` | `pypi` datasource | base of the PyPI JSON API (default `https://pypi.org`) |
| `GOPROXY`, `GONOPROXY`, `GOPRIVATE`, `GOMODCACHE` | `go` datasource | read via `go env -json` (the process environment when `go` is not on `PATH`). `GOMODCACHE`'s `cache/download/**/@v/*.info` files provide release times without network. |
| `GITHUB_ACTIONS`, `GITEA_ACTIONS`, `FORGEJO_ACTIONS`, `GITHUB_SERVER_URL`, `GITHUB_API_URL`, `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, `FORGEJO_SERVER_URL`, `FORGEJO_API_URL`, `FORGEJO_REPOSITORY` | all | platform detection: `FORGEJO_ACTIONS=true` → forgejo, `GITEA_ACTIONS=true` → gitea, `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` → github; the `FORGEJO_*` variables fall back to the `GITHUB_*` ones. `run` also detects from the `origin` remote; `plan`, `apply` and `explain` only from these variables. |
| `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, `GITEA_STEP_SUMMARY` | all | step summary file (see `deps help output`) |

On a 401 without a static token, git tag lookups call `git credential fill` once per host, with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and a 10s timeout. Every `git` process deps runs has `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, so deps never prompts. npm lookups use `.npmrc` `_authToken` entries, PyPI index lookups the index URL's userinfo (`https://user:token@host/simple`), and docker lookups the Docker credential chain (`~/.docker/config.json` and credential helpers).

Docker Hub limits anonymous pulls per IP address (`ratelimit-limit: 100;w=3600` at the time of writing) and counts every manifest GET; HEADs are free. deps resolves digests with HEADs and fetches a manifest only for release times. In repositories with many Docker Hub images, or on shared runner IPs, log in (`docker login`, or credentials for `docker.io` in `$DOCKER_CONFIG/config.json`). An exhausted quota fails the affected lookups at once with `rate limited by registry-1.docker.io`, instead of retrying until the window ends.

## Exit codes

Exit codes of every command. Also shown by `deps help exit-codes`.

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `0` | success, no errors |
| `1` | any error, including per-dependency lookup errors and per-PR errors (already printed as `error` lines), or a fatal error printed as `deps: <err>` |
| `2` | usage error: bad flag or argument, invalid `--log-level`/`--log-format`/`--platform`/`--concurrency`, invalid `DEPS_GIT_AUTHOR`, invalid `--trigger-schedule`/`DEPS_TRIGGER_SCHEDULE`, a `--signing-key`/`DEPS_SIGNING_KEY` that is no OpenSSH or armored OpenPGP private key, or any config error (parse error, unknown key, failed validation, unreadable `--config` file) |

## Output

Report lines, summary lines, diagnostics and the CI step summary. Also shown by `deps help output`.

Results go to stderr (the diff of `plan` and the report of `explain` go to stdout), in fixed-width lines:

```
update  <file>:<line>  <name>  <from> -> <to>  (<type>[, lockfile][, separate PR])[  security: <id>,<id>]
update  <lockfile>  lock file maintenance  (lockFileMaintenance, separate PR)   (with lockFileMaintenance)
skip    <file>:<line>  <name>  <reason>                       (with -v)
error   <message>
note    go.sum changes are computed by apply/run              (plan, when a gomod update exists)
note    package-lock.json changes are computed by apply/run   (plan, when an npm update exists)
note    Cargo.lock changes are computed by apply/run          (plan, when a cargo update exists)
note    uv.lock, poetry.lock, pdm.lock and Pipfile.lock changes are computed by apply/run   (plan, when a Python update exists)
note    --hash lines of requirements files are computed by apply/run   (plan, when a requirements file with --hash has an update)
note    .terraform.lock.hcl changes are computed by apply/run (plan, when a terraform update exists)
pr      <status>[, <automerge>]  <branch>  <title>  <url>     (run)
dashboard <status>  <title>  <url>                            (run, with dependencyDashboard)
```

- For digest and pin updates, `<from>`/`<to>` read `<version>@<sha7>`. A lockfile-only update (`, lockfile`) starts at the locked version and changes only the lockfile.
- Per-dependency errors read `<file>:<line>: <name>: <err>`; a fatal error is printed as `deps: <err>`.
- The PR, automerge and dashboard statuses are listed in `deps run --help`; the skip reasons in the managers reference.

**Summary lines:**

```
<n> updates in <m> files, <k> skipped, <e> errors                                                (plan, apply)
<c> created, <u> updated, <x> closed, <s> up-to-date, <k> skipped, <a> automerge, <e> errors     (run)
... (dry run: <w> would change, <m> would automerge)                                              (run --dry-run, appended)
```

`rebased` counts as updated. `<a>` counts auto-merge requests and direct merges (`automerge`, `merged`); the dashboard line is not counted.

**Diagnostics** are written with `log/slog` to stderr, filtered by `--log-level` and formatted by `--log-format`:

- `debug`: every HTTP request (credential-free URL), every `git`/`go`/`npm`/`cargo` process, credential-helper outcomes (never secrets), and per-dependency and per-PR decisions.
- `info`: the run trigger (`run`), the detected platform and how it was detected, the actions default host and its source (`actions default host host=<h> source=<s>`), phase counts and durations, and the bot's view of the repository.
- `warn` (the default): obsolete PRs left open because the run had errors, a schedule event whose cron cannot be read (every schedule matches), a dashboard skipped because issues are disabled, and dashboard labels that do not exist (Gitea/Forgejo).

**Summary block.** Before the summary line, a block starting with an empty line and `Summary: ` gives the overview:

```
Summary: <n> dependencies, <u> updates in <g> PRs[, PRs: <count> <status>, ...][, <p> held back by minimumReleaseAge], <k> skipped, <e> errors (<duration>)
  PR <branch>  <title>  [<status> <url>; <automerge>; waiting for <cron>]   (run; plan/apply: [automerge; schedule <crons>])
      <name>  <file>:<line>  <from> -> <to>  (<type>[, security: <id>,...])
  <status>  <branch>  <url>                                            (run: closed obsolete PRs and the dashboard)
  Held back by minimumReleaseAge:
      <name>  <file>:<line>  <version>  too new (released <date>, minimum <age>)
  Skipped (-v lists each dependency):
    <count>  <reason>  (<how to update>)
```

The PRs are the ones `run` opens: plan and apply group their updates the same way. Without updates, errors or PR actions, the headline reads `No updates: <n> dependencies up to date, <k> skipped.` Errors are not repeated; they are the `error` lines above.

**Step summary.** If `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (or else `GITEA_STEP_SUMMARY`) is set, the same summary is appended to that file as markdown, under `## deps <command>`: the headline, one section per PR with its branch, status and link (run), automerge and schedule, and a `| Dependency | File | From | To | Type |` table; other PR actions (closed PRs, the dashboard); held-back releases; skip reasons with counts and how to update, with the skipped dependencies in a collapsible `<details>`; and the errors in full.
